# Conformance

<!-- Generated by packages/llx-markdown/scripts/conformance.ts (`bun run conformance`). Do not edit: a test fails when this page is out of date. -->

llx-markdown reads Markdown with its own parser. This page is what that parser is held to: every example of the specifications is run, and every piece of syntax below is drawn and looked for in the page. The page is written by a script, and the test suite fails when it no longer matches the code.

| Suite | Examples | Pass |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| [CommonMark 0.31.2](https://spec.commonmark.org/0.31.2/) | 652 | 652 |
| [GitHub Flavored Markdown](https://github.github.com/gfm/), the extensions | 22 | 22 |
| [cmark-gfm](https://github.com/github/cmark-gfm)'s extension tests | 30 | 30 |

## GitHub Flavored Markdown

The examples of GitHub's specification that are about one of its extensions. (The rest of that document restates an older CommonMark, covered above at 0.31.2.) Task lists and footnotes have no examples there; cmark-gfm's own tests below cover them.

| Extension | Examples | Pass |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Tables | 8 | 8 |
| Strikethrough | 2 | 2 |
| Autolinks | 11 | 11 |
| Disallowed raw HTML | 1 | 1 |
| **All** | **22** | **22** |

## GitHub’s writing syntax

What [Basic writing and formatting syntax](https://docs.github.com/en/get-started/writing-on-github/getting-started-with-writing-and-formatting-on-github/basic-writing-and-formatting-syntax) lists, in its order. A dash is syntax that belongs to github.com (its users, issues and emoji), which a reply has no use for: it shows as written.

| Syntax | Supported | Note |
| --- | :-: | --- |
| Headings | ✓ |  |
| Bold | ✓ |  |
| Italic | ✓ |  |
| Strikethrough | ✓ |  |
| Bold with nested italic | ✓ |  |
| All bold and italic | ✓ |  |
| Subscript, superscript, underline | ✓ | raw HTML, sanitized |
| Quoting text | ✓ |  |
| Quoting code | ✓ |  |
| Supported color models (a swatch beside `#0969DA`) | — |  |
| Links | ✓ |  |
| Bare URLs become links | ✓ |  |
| Section links (heading ids) | ✓ | with `headingIds` |
| Custom anchors | ✓ | names are prefixed, as on GitHub |
| Line breaks: two spaces, backslash, `<br/>` | ✓ |  |
| Images | ✓ |  |
| The `<picture>` element | ✓ |  |
| Lists | ✓ |  |
| Nested lists | ✓ |  |
| Task lists | ✓ |  |
| Mentioning people and teams (`@octocat`) | — |  |
| Referencing issues and pull requests (`#12`) | — |  |
| Emoji shortcodes (`:+1:`) | — |  |
| Paragraphs | ✓ |  |
| Footnotes | ✓ |  |
| Alerts: note, tip, important, warning, caution | ✓ |  |
| Hiding content with comments | ✓ |  |
| Ignoring Markdown formatting (`\*`) | ✓ |  |

From the advanced pages of the same guide:

| Syntax | Supported | Note |
| --- | :-: | --- |
| Tables, with column alignment | ✓ |  |
| Collapsed sections (`<details>`) | ✓ | raw HTML, sanitized |
| Fenced code blocks with a language | ✓ |  |
| Diagrams (` ```mermaid `) | ✓ | drawn when `mermaid` is given |
| Mathematical expressions: `$…$`, `$$…$$`, ` ```math ` | ✓ | with `llx-markdown/math` |
| `<kbd>` keys | ✓ | raw HTML, sanitized |

## The dialect

What llx-markdown draws beyond Markdown; [Syntax](syntax.md) describes each form. Every form is plain Markdown to any other renderer.

| Syntax | Supported | Note |
| --- | :-: | --- |
| Callout with a title | ✓ |  |
| Steps | ✓ |  |
| Tabs | ✓ |  |
| Pros and cons | ✓ |  |
| Stats | ✓ |  |
| Details (a folded section) | ✓ |  |
| Sources | ✓ |  |
| Quote with its source | ✓ |  |
| Figure with a caption | ✓ |  |
| File tree | ✓ |  |
| Code block with a file name | ✓ |  |
| Diff | ✓ | colored with `llx-markdown/highlight` |
| Numbered sections | ✓ |  |
| Diagram | ✓ | drawn when `mermaid` is given |
| Math | ✓ | with `llx-markdown/math` |
